summary: A genuinely distinct, honestly-declared audio core sits atop a Program/performance layer that is implemented as tested pure functions but is entirely disconnected from the rendered instrument. Organ (B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe additive) and Synth (Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H) engines are real, category-distinct topologies wired to the keybed through one shared AudioContext and effect path, with real-boundary rendered-audio tests. But createProgramSystem/saveToCurrentSlot/selectProgram, addMorphDestination/clearMorphSource, bpmFromTapTimes, and engine.panic() are never imported or called by App/instrument/components: the panel's program buttons, Store, list view, scene toggles, morph-assign, split, tap-tempo, and Panic are silent no-ops, and several read keys mismatch their control IDs (program-split-on vs program-split, scene-i-active vs scene-i, unread synth-filter-type). All four technical gates pass. Visual fidelity is low versus the reference (generic slider grid, no LED drawbar graphs, truncated labels), narrow layout loses controls, and the Phase 2 and Phase 3 desktop captures are pixel-identical.

evidence: stage3-desktop.png is byte-identical to stage2-desktop.png (both 132439 bytes) and stage3-narrow.png identical to stage2-narrow.png (19803 bytes) per capture.json — no visible Phase 3 surface change captured.

Versus reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg the deck is a flat generic grid of range-slider knobs and buttons with truncated captions ('Piano Layer A En…', 'Master Fader Assig…'); the reference's clustered mini-controls, red LED drawbar graphs, and OLED program lists are absent.

Six sections are present in the documented order (Performance/Organ/Piano/Program/Synth/Layer Effects) with two OLEDs (Program, Synth), preserving gross layout and the deck/keybed split from Phase 1-2.

Program section renders program-btn-1..8, program-store, program-store-as, program-live-mode, program-scene-i/ii, program-split, program-morph-wheel/pedal, program-dial (hardware.ts:154-168) but none drive program state — programs.ts is never imported outside its own file/test (grep of src).

Scene/split/clock hardware state cannot reflect through the panel: control IDs program-scene-i/program-scene-ii/program-split do not match the keys read in presentationToAudioState (program-scene-i-active, program-split-on, program-clock-bpm), so those toggles change nothing.

Working state feedback is limited to the Program/Synth OLED text and per-control aria values; there are no split LEDs, dirty indicator, morph indicators, or drawbar LED graphs bound to real state in the rendered UI.

programs.ts implements 32 slots + 8 Live, Store/Store As with naming, dirty/edit-discard (selectProgram/saveToCurrentSlot/autoStoreLive) and 8 factory seeds, all covered by 11 tests in programs.test.ts.

None of it is reachable from the instrument: App.tsx -> Instrument -> SectionPanel -> DecorativeControl only calls instrument.interactControl, and useInstrument (state/instrument.ts) never imports programs.ts — createProgramSystem/loadCurrentSlot/selectProgram appear only inside programs.ts and its test (grep).

Clicking program-btn-1, program-store, program-live-mode, or program-dial merely toggles/sets a presentation value that presentationToAudioState ignores; there is no numeric list-view UI mounted at all.
Round-trip is therefore proven only at the pure-function level, not exercised through the running instrument as the rubric guidance requires.
Zones/splits (zones.ts: 11 positions C2-C7, Off/±6/±12 crossfades), morph interpolation (morph-clock.ts), and scenes are implemented and unit-tested (integration.test.ts).

Disconnected from the UI: addMorphDestination/clearMorphSource/bpmFromTapTimes are referenced only in morph-clock.ts + tests; there is no split-point editor, no morph-assign flow, and program-split/program-scene-* buttons are no-ops due to ID mismatches with the reader.
Transpose is the one performance control genuinely bound from the panel (program-transpose knob -> performance.transpose, clamped ±6 in control-bindings.ts:110).
Panic is not wired: engine.panic() is never called from useInstrument and there is no perf-panic click handler; tap-tempo clock (program-clock-bpm) is read but no control emits that key.

spawnOrganVoice (organ-voice.ts) implements per-model harmonic ratios and base waveforms (B3 sawtooth, Vox square, Farf boolean-drawbar square, Pipe sine), B3 percussion (2nd/3rd, soft/fast), key-click noise burst, and vib/chorus LFO; wired to the keybed via noteOn and a shared organ effect chain.

organ.test.ts proves distinct B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe spectra, drawbar changes altering rendered audio (signalsDiffer), percussion raising earlyRms, rotary routing changing the signal, and voice cleanup to zero.

Organ drawbars (organ-drawbar-1..9), model select, percussion, key-click, and rotary route ARE bound through presentationToAudioState (control-bindings.ts:67-85), so the organ plays and responds from the panel.
Gaps: vib/chorus C1-C3 vs V1-V3 depth is coarsely approximated, rotary acceleration is a shared ramp, and organ hardware-state feedback (drawbar LED graphs) is not rendered.

createSynthOscillators (synth-voice.ts) gives five categorically distinct topologies: single osc (Pure), hard-sync master+waveshaper (Sync), detuned Multi/Super stacks with count scaling on Osc Ctrl, and FM operator pair — category-correct Osc Ctrl (categoryOscCtrlEffect returns 0 for Pure).
createSynthFilter implements LP12/LP24/HP/BP with tracking, resonance, tanh drive; synth.test.ts proves category distinctness, filter freq/type/resonance and unison changes in rendered audio.

Panel gaps: synth-filter-type control exists (hardware.ts:189) but presentationToAudioState never reads it, and waveform category/voice-mode are not applied from the panel — synthCategoryFromPresentation/voiceModeFromPresentation are exported but never called, so category/filter-type only change via loaded programs, which themselves are unreachable.

Arp is shallow: scheduleArp spawns notes on an interval but never releases them (no note-off in the timer) risking stuck voices, and arp direction/hold/run/clock-sync are proven only for the pure buildArpSequence, not as rendered timed audio.

Engines are not renamed generic oscillators: organ uses additive harmonic stacks with per-model ratio tables (B3_RATIOS/VOX_RATIOS/PIPE_RATIOS) and Farf's binary drawbars; synth uses distinct sync/FM/supersaw topologies.
signalsDiffer assertions confirm B3 vs Vox vs Farf vs Pipe and Pure vs Sync and Multi vs FM-H render measurably different spectra (organ.test.ts, synth.test.ts).

Distinctness is proven for the sound engines that play from the keybed; it is not, however, reachable through the disconnected program/patch-selection UI, so audible variety in normal use depends on the few panel-bound controls.

PianoEngine builds one AudioContext with piano A/B, organ (shared), and synth A/B/C buses each feeding a LayerEffectChain into a single mixBus -> masterGain -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> context.destination (engine.ts:82-124).
A single SharedRotary instance is fed by all effect chains; integration.test.ts asserts getAudioContext() is identical across piano/organ/synth playback and organ layers share one chain.
Master level and per-layer levels are set via setTargetAtTime ramps with morph applied through applyMorphToValue; nothing bypasses the master path.
Minor smell: resolveEffectsForLayer('B') has a dead branch that always returns the global effects object, so per-layer-B effect differentiation is nominal.

MAX_POLYPHONY=32 with deterministic oldest-voice stealing, ramped attack/release, and a -3dB/20:1 limiter guard against clipping; allNotesOff/dispose return voice count to zero (organ.test.ts, engine.test.ts).
Capture console shows only benign repeated 'AudioContext was not allowed to start' autoplay warnings and no pageErrors (stage3-capture.json).

Arp scheduling never issues note-off for arp-spawned voices (scheduleArp in engine.ts), so held arp play accumulates voices until stealing kicks in — a latency/CPU and stuck-note risk under sustained integrated play.
Layered/split musical quality cannot be exercised through the UI because splits/scenes/programs are not wired, limiting demonstrable real-use load behavior.

audioToSerializable/applySerializableToAudio serialize all supported state except Master Level (honestly documented) and programs.test.ts proves slot round-trip restores piano/organ/synth/effects/split/scene/morph/clock fields.
Round-trip is never driven by the instrument: no UI path calls loadCurrentSlot/saveToCurrentSlot, so a user cannot save then reload a program and observe restored state.
restorePrograms/persistPrograms handle localStorage with 32/8 length guards, but persistence too is only invoked in tests, not from the mounted app.

The hardware.bindings test (integration.test.ts:123) only checks that isFunctionalControl(id) returns true, and isFunctionalControl merely prefix-matches ('program-'/'synth-'/'organ-'/'fx-') without proving any behavior — a rubber stamp.

Many prefix-'passing' controls are silent no-ops: program-btn-1..8, program-store/store-as, program-live-mode, program-scene-i/ii, program-split, program-morph-wheel/pedal, perf-panic, and synth-filter-type either read a mismatched key or are never read by presentationToAudioState.

The spec-excluded list (unsupported-controls.ts) is small (5 IDs) and does not account for the many program/performance controls that render but do nothing — those are undeclared no-op fallbacks, which the rubric scores 0.

Genuinely bound controls do exist (master level, mod wheel, transpose, piano type/level/octave, organ drawbars/model/percussion, synth level/osc-ctrl/filter-freq/res), so the layer is partially functional rather than wholly broken.

Engines can be layered from the keybed (noteOn fans out to piano A/B, organ A/B, synth A/B/C with zone/scene gating in engine.ts:350-399), so simultaneous multi-engine play works when layers are enabled via their bound enables.

Cross-system workflows that define Phase 3 — selecting a program, switching scenes, assigning a morph, editing a split, tapping the clock, hitting Panic — are not operable from the running instrument, so the pieces do not function as one system for a user.
Scene gating and morph are honored inside applyState only if state is mutated programmatically; the panel controls that should mutate them are disconnected.
Phase 1-2 tests are retained in feature-matrix.json (visual/key/interaction/accessibility/piano/effects IDs all present) and the verification record shows test/typecheck/lint/build all passed.
Piano library, two-layer behavior, velocity controls, pedals, fallback, and the effects graph/routing/processing remain covered by engine.test.ts (23 tests) with real offline-render assertions.
Narrow retention regressed: stage3-narrow.png collapses most controls into a few blobs with only two OLEDs legible, so responsive inspection of the surface is degraded rather than merely reflowed.
Inherited Phase 2 note: Grand/Upright/Electric remain synthesized (honestly declared), which is honest but does not meet the Phase 2 recorded-sample requirement — carried forward here.

Clear module boundaries: audio/ (engine, per-engine voices, effects-chain, zones, morph-clock, program-types), model/ (hardware, keyboard), state/ (programs, control-bindings, instrument), input/, components/ — with injectable AudioContext/timing/MIDI boundaries.
One-context routing, serializable program state, and per-engine voice modules are well-factored and extensible.

The central architectural flaw is that the state/program/performance layer is not connected to the presentation layer: useInstrument routes everything through a single presentationToAudioState mapping and never owns a ProgramSystemState, so an entire designed subsystem is dead relative to the UI.

Dead/loose ends: resolveEffectsForLayer's no-op branch, exported-but-unused synthCategoryFromPresentation/voiceModeFromPresentation, and control-ID/read-key mismatches indicate incomplete integration.

Audio tests are real-boundary and deterministic (renderOffline + rms/earlyRms/signalsDiffer), meaningfully proving engine distinctness, filter/drawbar/percussion/rotary effects, and cleanup — a genuine strength.

Coverage is skewed to pure functions and engine internals; there is essentially no UI-integration test (App.test.tsx is 1 trivial test), so the disconnection between controls and the program/performance workflow went unproven.
The hardware.bindings test asserts a prefix predicate rather than actual canonical behavior, giving false assurance for controls that do nothing.
Naming and modularity are otherwise clean and consistent (typed program-types, per-engine files), aiding maintainability.
Captures report no page errors at 1440x900 and 390x844; only benign autoplay AudioContext warnings appear (stage3-capture.json).
Voice/timer cleanup is handled (allNotesOff clears arp interval and sustained notes; dispose closes context and disconnects nodes) and tests confirm voice counts return to baseline.
setTargetAtTime ramps on levels/master avoid zipper noise and the limiter caps output; React state updates are memoized in useInstrument.
Residual risk: arp-spawned voices are never explicitly released, so long arp runs can grow node/voice counts until stealing intervenes.

issues: Program/performance subsystem (programs.ts, morph assignment, tap-clock, Panic) is fully implemented and unit-tested but never imported by App/instrument/components — program buttons, Store/Store As, Live mode, list view, scenes, morph-assign, split editor, tap-tempo, and Panic are non-functional from the running instrument.

Control-ID vs read-key mismatches make several panel controls silent no-ops: program-split (read as program-split-on), program-scene-i/ii (read as *-active), program-clock-bpm (no emitting control), and synth-filter-type is never read.

hardware.bindings test only checks a prefix predicate (isFunctionalControl) and does not prove canonical behavior, so many no-op controls pass; undeclared no-op fallbacks are not listed as unsupported.
Arp scheduling (scheduleArp) spawns notes on a timer but never issues note-off for them, risking stuck/accumulating voices under sustained arp play.
Visual fidelity is low versus reference (generic slider grid, truncated labels, no LED drawbar graphs); Phase 2 and Phase 3 captures are byte-identical and narrow layout drops most controls.
